title: BP vs Buckler 1987
authority: National Police Chiefs' Council (for the National Counter Terrorism Security Office)

messages.from: National Police Chiefs' Council (for the National Counter Terrorism Security Office)
messages.summary: Automated receipt from the NPCC FOI mailbox.
messages.body_public:
Thank you for your email to the NPCC FOI Team at the National Police
Freedom of information and Data Protection Unit (NPFDU).
If your email constitutes a Freedom of Information request, you will
receive a separate formal acknowledgement confirming receipt and providing
a case reference number for use in all future correspondence.
All requests will be processed in accordance with the Freedom of
Information legislation.
Under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act, you have a right to request
access to personal data related to you from an organisation. If this is
what you require you will need to contact a local force or ACRO Criminal
Records Office, rather than the NPCC.
Similary, if you require your data held on the Police National Computer
(the central record of conviction and non-conviction outcomes), [1]ACRO
Criminal Records Office manage these requests on behalf of the NPCC so you
can obtain this data from them. To make your request, you will need to use
the ACRO subject access online process via
[2]
https://www.acro.police.uk/s/acro-servic...
NPCC Freedom of Information Officers & Decision Makers
A | NPFDU PO Bx 841, Fareham, Hampshire, PO14 9FS
E | [3][email address]
W| [4]www.npcc.police.uk

messages.from: National Police Chiefs' Council (for the National Counter Terrorism Security Office)
messages.summary: Reply: no request for recorded information identified, so no action under the Act (FOI 3043/2026).
messages.body_public:
Thank you for your correspondence.
The Freedom of Information Act 2000 provides a right of access to recorded information held by public authorities.
Having reviewed your correspondence, we have been unable to identify a request for recorded information under the Act. Consequently, we are unable to process this correspondence as a Freedom of Information request.
No further action will be taken in relation to this matter under the Freedom of Information Act 2000.
NPCC Freedom of Information Officers & Decision Maker
National Police FOI & DP Central Referral Unit (NPFDU)

E | [email address]

messages.from: National Police Chiefs' Council (for the National Counter Terrorism Security Office)
messages.summary: Confirms the correspondence is treated as both a new request and an internal review.
messages.body_public:
Good Morning
We acknowledge receipt of your correspondence as both a Freedom of Information request and a request for internal review. We will conduct a review of the decision communicated on 2 September 2026 and will separately consider whether any information falling within the scope of your request is held by the NPCC, including any relevant predecessor records. If no information is held, we will explain this and, where possible, provide advice and assistance regarding other bodies that may hold relevant records.
A formal acknowledgement of your FOI request, and your request for an Internal Review have been sent this morning.
Kind regards.
NPCC Freedom of Information Officers & Decision Maker
National Police FOI & DP Central Referral Unit (NPFDU)
